ambiguities.description: FR4 defines token-based access as V2 priority under Authentication, while FR68 defines shareable link generation under Sharing & Export. The boundary between authentication-level token access (FR4) and link generation UX (FR68) is unclear. Who generates the token — the auth system or a sharing service? What happens when an authenticated user accesses a shared link for their own org's report?

FR20 defines COMPLETED_PARTIAL when 'some LLMs fail' but does not specify the user experience when viewing partial results. Which dashboard sections show partial data? Are metrics recalculated excluding failed LLMs? Is the user warned per-widget that data is incomplete? The LLM filter behavior with failed engines is unspecified.

FR38 defines 8 improvement area types with severity thresholds (Critical <25%, Warning <40%, Info <50%) but the special rule 'all competitive improvements cleared when global favorability >= 95%' lacks precision: does 'global favorability' mean across all LLMs, all markets, or the current filter selection? The 'max 3 reputation items per category' rule does not specify the selection criteria when more than 3 exist.

FR17 validates quotas at configuration time, and FR51 consumes +1 brand_market on market addition. Edge case: what happens if two editors from the same org simultaneously add markets that would exceed quota? The 'submission-time quota check' in FR17 applies to wizard, but FR51's Manage Scope flow does not explicitly mention a second check. Race condition between concurrent editors is unspecified.

FR60 states weekly execution uses 'same day/time as initial configuration (or last edit)'. FR54 says changes saved immediately but applied on next execution. If an editor modifies config at 3pm Wednesday and the report was initially configured at 10am Monday, does the weekly schedule shift to Wednesday 3pm? The 'or last edit' clause creates ambiguity about schedule drift.

FR31 defines AI Perception Summary with '3 bullet points (150 chars max)' but does not specify: max per bullet or max total? What language is the summary generated in — primary market language or the user's UI language? What happens if the LLM generates more than 3 bullets or exceeds the character limit?

FR14 (wizard) states 'if user disables all, system auto-enables all' as a fallback. FR57 (manage scope) states 'min 1 engine must remain active'. These are two different enforcement strategies for the same constraint (min 1 LLM). The wizard allows disabling all then auto-corrects, while manage scope prevents the last disable. Inconsistent UX pattern.

FR53 auto-detects competitors from visibility rankings. FR53b allows manual competitor addition merged with auto-detected ones. Edge case: if auto-detection finds 10 competitors and the max_competitors_per_category is 10, can the user still add manual competitors? Does manual addition override auto-detected ones or are they additive up to cap? Priority between manual and auto-detected is unspecified.

FR30 specifies soft delete with 'shared links for deleted reports return 404'. But soft delete typically means data is retained. Is there a hard delete after a retention period? Can a deleted report be restored? What happens to scheduled weekly execution for a soft-deleted report — is it cancelled?

FR20e defines brand logo display using Brandfetch with 'first-letter avatar if logo unavailable'. But it does not specify: what domain is used to look up competitor logos (auto-detected competitors may not have a known domain)? How are logos cached? What is the fallback for brands with no domain at all (custom brands from FR5)?

FR8 states 'Empty category list blocks navigation to Review Prompts' but does not specify what happens if the AI discovery API is unavailable or times out. Is the user blocked entirely, or can they proceed with only custom categories (FR9)? The error/timeout handling for AI category discovery is unspecified.

FR65 states 'minimum retention: 12 months' and FR66 provides previous/next navigation. Edge case: for a weekly execution, 12 months = ~52 snapshots. Is there a maximum snapshot limit? What happens at month 13 — is the oldest snapshot auto-purged? Does navigation handle gaps (skipped weeks due to failures)?

epics_without_ac.risk: HIGH - Auth & access is the entry gate for all users. Without formal AC, test cases for Auth0 integration, role-based access (Editor vs Reader), org context resolution, and module activation redirect logic must be derived entirely from PRD FR0-FR3. Risk of missing edge cases: expired tokens, multi-org users, concurrent sessions, SSO failure handling.

HIGH - The wizard is the primary onboarding flow with 7 stories covering 13 FRs. Without formal AC, validation rules (quota limits, duplicate detection, min/max constraints), AI interaction patterns (Brandfetch, category discovery, auto-translation), and atomic save behavior must be inferred from PRD. Critical risk areas: quota race conditions (FR17), wizard state persistence across steps, auto-punctuation edge cases (FR11).

HIGH - The analysis pipeline is the core value engine with 8 stories covering 16 FRs including parallel LLM execution, real-time progress, email notifications, and weekly scheduling. Without formal AC, error handling (circuit breaker, retry logic), status transitions (COMPLETED/COMPLETED_PARTIAL/FAILED), and notification timing (<5 min) are untestable against Jira. Must rely entirely on PRD.

MEDIUM - Dashboard is the primary read surface with 10 stories covering 19 FRs. Stories are well-decomposed (one per widget/feature), which partially compensates for missing AC. However, metric calculation formulas (FR79-FR84), filter interaction behavior, and perception summary caching rules need PRD-based validation. KPI threshold values and matrix quadrant definitions are specified in PRD but not in Jira.

summary.uncovered_feature_area: Sharing & Export (FR4, FR68-FR73) — 7 FRs with no dedicated Epic
key_risks: Sharing & Export is a complete backlog gap — 7 V2 FRs (FR4, FR68-FR73) have no Epic, no stories, and no AC. Business flow BF-004 (Report Sharing) is entirely unimplemented in Jira.
5 of 8 Epics (GEO-105, GEO-104, GEO-103, GEO-102, GEO-101) lack formal acceptance criteria in Jira. Test case generation must rely on PRD functional requirements as the sole source of truth.
GEO-103 (Pipeline) is the highest-risk Epic: 16 FRs, 0 AC, complex error handling (circuit breaker, partial failure), real-time progress, and email notification timing constraints.
Quota race condition (AMB-004) between wizard (FR17) and manage scope (FR51) is a concurrency risk with no specified resolution strategy.
LLM min-1 enforcement (AMB-007) uses contradictory patterns: auto-enable-all in wizard vs prevent-last-disable in manage scope.

recommendation_details: Coverage is 92.1% (82/89 FRs) but the Sharing & Export gap (7 FRs) represents a full feature area missing from Jira. Additionally, 5 of 8 Epics lack formal AC, forcing test case generation to rely solely on PRD. Before generating test cases: (1) Confirm whether Sharing & Export is intentionally deferred or needs a new Epic (GEO-098?). (2) Request AC formalization for GEO-105 (Auth), GEO-104 (Wizard), and GEO-103 (Pipeline) — the three highest-risk Epics. (3) Resolve AMB-004 (quota race condition) and AMB-007 (LLM min-1 contradiction) as they affect test case expected behavior. If clarification is not available, test cases can proceed using PRD as authoritative source, but ambiguities should be flagged as 'assumption-based' in each affected test case.
